prompt: evals/datasets/store_sales.csv has weekly sales for 20 stores for about 2 years. Inventory planning needs an 8-week-ahead forecast per store. Build the best forecasting approach you can and tell me how accurate to expect it to be.

assertions.text: inventory_end is never used for the week being forecast; if used at all, only values at or before the forecast origin are used, and the report explains why that is available at forecast time
The five -1 sales values are treated as missing or invalid, not as real sales
Duplicate (store_id, week_start) rows are detected and removed
The missing weeks for S03 are detected and the series is reindexed to a regular weekly grid before modelling
The S07 level shift and/or the intermittent S19 series are detected and handled or explicitly discussed
Accuracy is estimated with a time-ordered backtest (rolling or expanding origin) using an 8-week horizon; no shuffled K-fold is used on the time series
A seasonal naive (lag-52) or last-value baseline is reported with the same metric as the final approach
A scale-free metric (MASE, sMAPE, WAPE, or RMSSE) is reported, overall and ideally by horizon or by store
promo and holiday_week are used as known-future covariates, or the report explains why not; avg_temp_c is not treated as known in the future without comment
forecast.csv contains 20 stores x 8 future weeks with non-negative values
At least two forecasting approaches are compared in the backtest with spread across origins reported
For each major stage the report states what was applied and why, and what was considered but skipped and why
